english: The warriors killed the king. Then his son grew up and became strong. Then he spoke to his mother: "Whoever killed my father, to him I shall give vengeance (payment)." Then he rode to them with his horse(s). Then they saw him coming. Then he struck them down. Then they fell down, and he gave them their punishment. Then he became king, and his fame became great.
uncertain: h₁éḱwoh₁ ... tóns wéǵʰet: read as INS 'with his horse(s) he drove/rode to them' (tóns ACC goal); if h₁éḱwoh₁ is NOM.DU 'his two horses' as subject, 3SG wéǵʰet would not agree and tóns 'them' would be odd (expected tóm 'him')
kʷoynéh₂m: 'payment' vs 'punishment, vengeance'; chose vengeance/punishment
gʷʰént: PST 'was striking/slaying', rendered 'killed'/'struck down'

english: A man worked ten years in a far-off field. Then the years were long. Then he came to his hill. A dog was lying there. The dog saw him and recognized him. Then it came to him and died. His wife was sitting there. He went to her, but she did not recognize him. Then he said: "Wife, do you not recognize me? I know you." Then the two rejoiced.
uncertain: h₁ést: 'was' (PST of h₁esti) vs AOR 'threw'; 'was' fits
dweh₂róy h₂éǵroy: LOC 'in a far/long field'
kólHonm̥: 'hill' (ACC goal), perhaps his home hill
só ... mért: 'it (the dog) died'; só could also be the man, but the dog reading fits

english: The gods sat down on the mountain. Then Father Dyeus said: "Who will protect mortals?" Then Dawn said: "I will protect them." Then Earth said: "I will protect them from below." Then Fire spoke: "I will protect them in the field." "Your word is good." Then Mother Earth heard them and rejoiced. Then they drank sweet water.
uncertain: péruni: LOC 'on the rock/mountain'
wékʷos wos h₁wésu h₁ésti: speaker not marked, presumably Dyeus to the three
tóy ... ph₃ént: 'they' = probably the mortals (or the gods)

english: The men laid the man down. Then they burned him with fire. The fire was red. His father stood at the fire, and his wife was looking at the fire. Then he said to them: "Give him a famous name!" Then they gave him a famous name. Then he gave them ten cattle. "He has imperishable fame." Death had seized him, but his fame did not perish.
uncertain: logʰéyont: 'laid (to rest)', a funeral
dʰh₁té: AOR.2PL/IMP.2PL of dʰeh₁ 'put, place', read as imperative 'give (him a name)'
h₁ésti ... tósmey: present-tense speech or narrator comment: 'there is imperishable fame for him'
gʷh₂tós: lexicon gives 'death' (NOM)

english: The Sun's daughter went to the water. The water was great, and she sank down in it. She became afraid and said: "Sons of Dyeus, hear me! Rescue me from the water!" The two heard her. Then they arrived on their chariot, and two swift horses were drawing it. Then they drew her out of the water and set her on the chariot. Then they brought her to the Sun. It rejoiced and said: "You two have rescued my daughter. Protect men!"
uncertain: diwés ... suHnúh₁: VOC.DU 'two sons of Dyeus' (the divine twins)
tóm (after the horses): masc ACC 'it' = the chariot (kʷékʷlos)
tód méwdt: neuter tód = the Sun (sóh₂wl̥ is neuter)
wédʰetām: 'led/brought' (wedʰ- 'lead') vs homonym 'bind, marry'; 'brought' fits

english: A great serpent lay on the mountain and held the rivers shut up inside. The earth and the cattle were thirsty. Then the gods said to the hero: "Slay the serpent! Free them!" Then he took his spear and went forward. The serpent saw him coming. Then he struck the serpent. He split the rock apart. Then the rivers came out and the earth drank water. Then the gods gave him imperishable fame.
uncertain: ḱélet ... h₁n̥dóm: 'was covering/keeping inside'
pérwr̥: 'rock/mountain' vs 'ford'; rock fits
tóns spr̥dʰí: masc ACC.PL 'free them' = the rivers/cattle

english: The warriors seized the queen and drove her and the cattle away. Then the queen's brother said to a man: "Free her! I will give you a great reward." Then he tracked them. He came to the ford and saw them sitting. Then he killed them. Then the queen saw him, and he freed her. Then he drove them (the cattle) back, and he led her to her brother, who gave him the reward. Then imperishable fame came to him.
uncertain: pérwr̥: 'ford, crossing' vs 'rock'; either works
h₁élh₂t: AOR.3SG after a 3PL subject ('they seized ... and drove'); could be one warrior driving or a slip for 3PL
ǵʰéyt tóns h₂epó: 'drove them away/back', presumably the cattle
misfit: h₁élh₂t: 3SG verb coordinated with 3PL subject Hyudʰsmṓs ... lm̥bʰént (expected 3PL)

english: A wolf saw a horse. Then the wolf said: "Horse, I will eat you." Then the horse said: "Wolf, look at my heel (hoof)! Then eat me." Then the wolf went in front and looked at the horse's heel. Then the horse struck the wolf with its heel. The wolf fell down and said: "The horse's words were sweet, and the horse's heel struck me. Whoever trusts sweet words, death finds him."
uncertain: tpḗrsneh₂: 'heel', here likely 'hoof'
h₂énti: 'in front, facing'
h₁éḱwosyo wékʷōs ... h₁ést: neuter plural with singular verb, which is regular

english: The Sun gave his daughter to a man and gave him ten cattle. Then he became the Sun's son-in-law. He drove two swift horses. The two drew the chariot, and she sat in it. Then his mother saw her. The mother said: "Daughter, be dear to me! Be my son's wife!" "I will be (his) wife." May the gods protect the two of them, and may the two live long.
uncertain: tósyo méh₂tēr: 'his mother' = the groom's mother
priHéh₂: 'dear, beloved'
h₁opéyet: 'gave, handed over'

english: The king wished for a son.
uncertain: wl̥nh₁to: the analyzer links it to wl̥néh₃ti 'to hit, strike' ('the king struck his son'), but the h₁ and the middle voice point to welh₁- 'to choose, want' (lexicon has pie-root-welh1-choose); chose 'wished for'
h₃rḗḱs: spelled with ḱ, a variant of h₃rḗǵs 'king'

english: The sheep and the horses.
uncertain: owis eḱwōskʷe: different (laryngeal-less) orthography, not analyzed; owis 'sheep', eḱwōs 'horses' + -kʷe 'and'; looks like a title

english: A serpent lay on the hill and was devouring the queen's cattle. Then the queen said to the warriors: "Who will slay the serpent?" They were afraid. Then a man stood up and said: "I will slay the serpent." "If you slay the serpent, I will give you my daughter." Then he went forward. The serpent saw him coming. Then he struck the serpent down. Then the queen gave him her daughter, and great fame came to him.
uncertain: h₁yód ... méne toy dʰugh₂térm̥ déh₃oh₂: speaker not marked, presumably the queen
gʷʰént: PST 'was striking/slaying', rendered 'struck down'

english: A man and another (man) arrived at a field. They stood facing each other. Then the other said: "Who are you?" "I am the king's son. Whoever is afraid, let him go away." Then the other threw his spear, and the spear went past him. Then he threw his spear, and the spear pierced the other's heart. He fell down and died. Then he took the other's two horses and drove them away. And imperishable fame arose for him.
uncertain: dʰégʷʰh₂t: 'came near, almost reached, passed by', so the spear missed
séh₁t / léh₁t: both 'let go', i.e. threw (the spear)

english: The father said to his son: "Hear my words. Guard the cattle and the sheep. Do not steal another man's cattle. Whoever seeks fame, let him be good. Death comes to men. My son, do not be afraid." He heard those words and said: "I will do that." Then he became great, and his name became famous.
uncertain: gʷémt mértis wiHróns: AOR 'death has come to men', gnomic
téh₂: neuter plural 'those things'
misfit: h₁sdʰí: 2SG imperative 'be!' with 3SG subject só (the correlative of h₁yós ... h₂isḱḗti); 3SG imperative h₁éstu expected

english: The gods' cattle were on the hill. When it grew dark there, a serpent stole the cattle and drove them into the rock. When dawn broke, they searched for the cattle. Then a god said: "Our cattle are gone. Who stole them?" Then a man said: "The serpent stole them. I will track the cattle." Then he came to the rock and split it open. The serpent became afraid, and he killed the serpent. Then the cattle came out. May Father Dyeus, giver of good things, protect the cattle.
uncertain: h₂wést: 'dawn shone/broke' (h₂west- 'become bright at dawn')
tóy ... h₂isḱónt: 'they' = the gods

english: A mortal lay on the ground. Death came to him, and he died. Then his brother saw him lying there and was afraid. He said to the gods: "He is lying there and does not see me." Then they said: "Mortals die. Death comes to men. Good fame does not perish." Then they gave him a famous name, and his name became great.
uncertain: ǵʰémi: LOC 'on the ground' (analyzer: dʰéǵʰōm)
misfit: mr̥wé: AOR.1DU 'we two died' with NOM.PL subject mórtōs 'mortals'; a 3PL form ('mortals die') is expected

english: The king's brother seized the two sons and laid them on the ground. Then he went away. A she-wolf heard the two, came to them, and nursed them. Then a shepherd saw them. They grew up and became strong. Then the two said to the shepherd: "Who is our father?" He said: "The king is your father. His brother seized you two." Then the two went to him and killed him. And the two became famous.
uncertain: nos / wos: plural 'our/your' used for a pair, while the next sentence has dual woh₃; the closed class has no dual genitive, so this is probably acceptable
h₂élet: 'was nourishing', i.e. nursed

english: Fire left the gods and sank down into the waters. They searched for him: "Where is Fire?" Fire was red (glowing). Then a fish saw him in the water and said: "He is in the waters." Then they went to the waters and said: "Agni, come out! We will give you a famous name." Then Fire came out of the water. They took him and brought him to mortals. Now mortals cook with fire. Agni, giver of good things, protect us!
uncertain: deywóybʰos: ABL.PL 'from the gods' (also DAT)
skʷént: sekʷ- 'say' (as introducing the speech) vs 'follow'; chose 'said'
h₁n̥gʷnís h₁rowdʰós h₁ést: 'Fire was red' reads oddly here; perhaps 'glowing (in the water)'
h₁pént: AOR.3PL of h₁ep- 'seize, take'
misfit: wédney: DAT.SG 'to/for the water' used where location 'in the water' is meant (LOC expected)

english: A man and his brother went into battle on a chariot. His brother was driving the two swift horses. Then the two reached the warriors. He was striking them. Then another (warrior) threw his spear, and the spear pierced the brother's heart. He fell down from the chariot. Then the man took the two (horses) and drove them forward. He carried him out of the battle and said: "My brother, you are gone. Your fame will not perish."
uncertain: stunédt só tóns: 'he' = probably the man (or the brother)
sléh₂gʷt só tóh₁: 'took the two', i.e. the horses (dual)
kéh₃tum: ACC goal 'into battle'; kh₃téws ABL 'out of battle'

english: A wife sat on a hill and kept looking at the path. The years went by. Her heart was trembling. Then she said: "Dawn, bring my husband to me! You have seen the fields and the waters. Have you seen him?" "I have seen him. He is coming on the path." Then the wife saw him coming. She recognized him, and her heart rejoiced. Then he went to her, and the two rejoiced.
uncertain: méne wiHróm: 'my husband'
wétōs h₁éyt: neuter plural with singular verb, 'the years went by'
misfit: gʷm̥sḱétes: 2DU/3DU 'you two / they two are coming', but only the one man (tóm) is meant; 3SG gʷm̥sḱéti expected

english: A man was driving his two horses into battle. Then the left horse stopped, and it said to him: "We will carry you out of the battle. Death is before you." "Horse, I know that. Death is before me. You two swift horses, carry me into battle!" Then the two horses carried him into battle. A spear pierced his heart, and he fell from the chariot. Then imperishable fame came to him.
uncertain: kh₃téws: GEN/ABL; read as ABL 'out of/away from the battle'
bʰérōmes: 1PL subjunctive 'we will carry' from one speaking horse for the pair; a 1DU might be expected
sth₂éh₁yet: 'stood (still)', i.e. stopped

english: Dyeus lay upon the earth. Men lived between them, and it was dark there. A man grew strong. Then he stood up and pushed the two apart. Dyeus was above, and Earth was below. Then it grew bright above, and they looked around. "Our father Dyeus, Mother Earth, hear (us)!" The two heard us.
uncertain: ḱlutā́m tóh₁ n̥smé: AOR.3DU 'the two heard us' (ḱlutā́m as fem ACC 'famous' does not fit)
ḱlutóm: IMP.2DU 'hear, you two'

english: When it grew dark on the hill, the warriors lay down on the ground. But a man stayed awake. He heard wolves, and the wolves came forward. He said to them: "Warriors, wake up! Take your spears!" They woke up. A wolf seized a sheep. Then they killed the wolves. The she-wolf went away. Then it grew light above. He looked around: the sheep were alive.
uncertain: bʰéwdʰet: PST 'was awake/watchful'

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field (plain).
uncertain: different orthography: ḱeḱluwōs PRF ACT PTCP 'having heard'; aǵrom 'field' ACC goal; ebʰuget augmented past of bʰewg- 'flee', not in the analyzer

english: A snake lay out in the winter cold. The snake became cold. A shepherd saw the snake and picked it up. He was warming it with fire. The snake became warm. Then the snake seized (bit) him. He said: "I was warming you with fire, and you seize me?" "I am a snake." Then it killed him. Do not warm a snake. Whoever warms a snake, the snake will kill him.
uncertain: ǵʰyémi: LOC 'in winter/in the frost'
h₁épt: 'seized', here 'bit'

english: Dawn, driving the red cattle, comes from the mountain. Mortals have woken. Dogs hear her, and the wolves have gone away. The shepherd leads his sheep forth, and they drink water. She gives them good things. Her path is short. The Sun looks at her, and she departs. Dawn, daughter of Dyeus, drive the red cattle for us! Hear us!
uncertain: péruns: ABL 'from the rock/mountain'
litént: AOR 'went away' mixed with present tense

english: A mortal died. He went along the path and came to the river. Two dogs with four eyes were lying there. The two saw him, and he said: "Dogs, let me go!" The two heard his famous name, and they let him go. Then he crossed it and came to the gods. And they gave him good things.
uncertain: ḱlutā́m: AOR.3DU 'the two heard' (fem ACC 'famous' would not agree with neuter h₁nómn̥)
gʷéh₂t tód pér: 'went through/across it' (the river)
misfit: h₁r̥té: AOR/IMP 2PL in third-person singular narration; 3SG h₁ért 'he arrived' expected

english: A man and a warrior stood facing each other. The warrior said: "You are a wolf. You steal cattle. Your heart is a sheep's heart. Your words are sweet, and your spear is short. My spear is long." Then the man said: "Come across the river!" Then a mortal came between them and said: "Go away from this, you two!" And the two went away.
uncertain: h₂éwis: NOM 'bird' or GEN of h₂ówis 'sheep'; the frame 'your heart is X's heart' needs a genitive, so 'sheep's'
só mléwHt: 'he' = the man (wiHrós)
tósmōd h₂epó: 'away from that (fight)'
